input.strategy_title: Idle resource reporting in the web console
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Cluster administrators cannot see which resources are sitting idle: workbenches
nobody has touched in weeks keep their volumes and reservations, and old
pipeline runs accumulate storage. Admins ask for a single report in the RHOAI
web console showing idle and stale resources per project so they can reclaim
capacity with confidence. The notebook controller already tracks last-activity
timestamps, and Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion metadata — the data
exists; it is just not surfaced anywhere.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | Administrators can export either report as CSV. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps. |

## Affected Components

- RHOAI web console
- Notebook controller
- Kubeflow Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources
- Cost/chargeback calculations

## Open Questions

None.

# Idle and stale resource reports in the RHOAI web console

## Description

This epic delivers per-project idle-resource reporting in the RHOAI web console:
a report of idle workbenches (with last activity, owner, and reserved resources)
and a report of stale pipeline runs (completed runs older than a configurable
age, with retained artifacts). Administrators can export either report as CSV so
they can reclaim capacity with confidence. All source data already exists in the
platform — the notebook controller's activity tracking and Kubeflow Pipelines
run metadata — so this epic surfaces it in the console without code changes to
those components.

## Scope

- Per-project idle-workbench report in the console: per workbench, show last
  activity (sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking), owner,
  and reserved resources (volumes, reservations).
- Stale pipeline-run report in the console: completed pipeline runs older than a
  configurable age, with their retained artifacts, sourced from Kubeflow
  Pipelines run metadata.
- Configurable age threshold for pipeline-run staleness.
- CSV export of either report.
- Discover and consume the notebook-controller activity data and the Kubeflow
  Pipelines run metadata through surfaces the console can read (the console uses
  the Kubernetes API; it owns no data plane).
- Out of scope: automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources, and
  cost/chargeback calculations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches with differing activity, the console
  shows a per-project idle-workbench report listing each workbench's last
  activity, owner, and reserved resources, with last activity sourced from the
  notebook controller's activity tracking.
- Given a project with completed pipeline runs, the console shows a stale
  pipeline-run report listing completed runs older than the configured age with
  their retained artifacts, sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- The stale-run age threshold is configurable.
- Given either report, an administrator can export it as CSV.
- The notebook controller and Kubeflow Pipelines operate without code changes
  for this reporting (passive validation): the reports read their data through
  Kubernetes-API-accessible surfaces, and existing console views of workbenches
  and pipeline runs continue to work.
- No automated reclamation/deletion or cost/chargeback functionality is
  introduced.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved
  resources) sourced from notebook controller activity tracking.
- HLR-2 (P1): stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a
  configurable age with retained artifacts) sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run
  metadata.
- HLR-3 (P2, bundled): CSV export of either report — bundled because it renders
  the same report data through the same report views; not separately
  schedulable.

# Document the idle resource reports and safe reclamation steps

## Description

This epic delivers administrator documentation for the console's idle-resource
reporting capability: what the idle-workbench and stale pipeline-run reports
show, where their data comes from, how to configure the staleness age, how to
use CSV export, and the steps to safely reclaim the capacity the reports
identify. It is authored through the Red Hat docs content process after the
console capability is implemented.

## Scope

Content outline:

- New documentation topics explaining the per-project idle-workbench report:
  columns (last activity, owner, reserved resources), its sourcing from the
  notebook controller's activity tracking, and how to read it.
- New documentation topics explaining the stale pipeline-run report: what
  "stale" means, the configurable age threshold and how to change it, retained
  artifacts, and its sourcing from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- Guidance for using CSV export of either report.
- Safe reclamation steps for administrators: what the reports indicate can be
  reclaimed, cautions and ordering of steps, and an explicit statement that the
  platform does not automatically reclaim or delete idle resources (manual,
  administrator-driven action only).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation explains both reports, their columns and data sources, the
  configurable stale-run age, and CSV export.
- Documentation includes safe reclamation steps consistent with the strategy's
  out-of-scope boundary (no automated reclamation or deletion; no
  cost/chargeback).
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented console
  capability and its statements match the shipped behavior (accuracy validated
  against the implementation).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps.
